claims.capability: Menu configuration uses nested menus, groups, optional subgroups, items, modifier groups and modifiers.
claims.merchant_outcome: Organize offerings so employees and supported ordering channels can locate and customize them.
claims.trigger: Creating or changing catalog structure
claims.behavior: Menus contain groups; groups can contain subgroups and items; groups or items can carry modifier groups, and modifiers can contain nested modifier groups. Toast Online Ordering and Mobile Order & Pay flatten subgroup items into the parent group presentation.
claims.preconditions: Toast menu entities configured in the platform; channel support can vary by Toast product.
claims.qualifiers: Guide describes English (United States); menu manager at time of documentation did not support subgroups or nested modifier groups, while classic menu workflow supported them.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: A channel without subgroup support changes the display hierarchy; verify every target channel after restructuring.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could make catalog structure and channel-specific rendering differences easier to preview before publication; measure menu setup time and ordering errors.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Catalog organization is independent of payment funding; Bitcoin acceptance does not intrinsically improve this job.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No payment-related benefit is evidenced here; any integration could add another channel compatibility surface.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure a menu with subgroup and nested modifier structures; verify the classic and menu manager capabilities and record rendered structure across POS, online ordering and Mobile Order & Pay.

claims.capability: Menu items and modifier entities can be reused across selected parts of a menu hierarchy.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reduce repeated configuration for shared items or modifier choices.
claims.trigger: Applying an existing item or modifier group to more than one menu entity
claims.behavior: Menu items may appear in multiple menu groups; modifier groups can be shared across groups or items; modifiers can be shared across modifier groups. Menu groups themselves cannot be shared among menus. Existing menu groups/items may be reused as modifier groups/modifiers, respectively.
claims.preconditions: Entity exists in the Toast menu configuration.
claims.qualifiers: Toast Platform Guide menu hierarchy behavior.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Shared entities may affect multiple uses when edited; check each parent use before republishing.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could show reuse impact and dependent menus before edits; measure accidental downstream menu changes.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Payment rail choice does not affect entity reuse; no direct Bitcoin benefit is implied.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Additional payment channels could create separate price/display configuration work if not normalized.
claims.acceptance_test: Reuse one item and modifier group across menu parents, edit the shared entity, and verify visible dependent uses are identified before publication.

claims.capability: Menu builder settings include schedule, channel visibility, prep station, course, sales category and tax configuration.
claims.merchant_outcome: Control when and where a menu is offered and connect menu entities with kitchen and reporting configuration.
claims.trigger: Creating or editing a menu in Menu Builder
claims.behavior: An administrator can configure days/times and ordering channel visibility along with kitchen prep, course, sales category and tax settings. Multi-location schedules use each location's local time.
claims.preconditions: Uses the documented menu builder workflow, not necessarily classic Edit menus or Menu Manager.
claims.qualifiers: Menu builder source; tax outcomes and advanced pricing rules were not examined in this claim.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: A schedule intended as one shared clock time may differ by location because local time applies; verify location-level behavior.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could provide a cross-location schedule preview with explicit time zones; measure missed or premature menu availability.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Menu scheduling and routing are separate from the funding instrument.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin payment availability would not resolve schedule or channel configuration needs.
claims.acceptance_test: Set a schedule for two locations in different time zones and verify menu visibility by channel at the intended local times.

claims.capability: Saved configuration may need publication before it appears on POS devices or in API results.
claims.merchant_outcome: Make prepared menu and other location configuration changes live for staff, guests and integrations.
claims.trigger: Saving an applicable configuration change
claims.behavior: Toast documents that new menu items or price changes may not appear on POS devices or API results until published; multi-location operators must publish to each applicable location. Publishing has no rollback; reverting requires manually restoring configuration and publishing again.
claims.preconditions: Change type requires publishing; user has publishing permission and relevant locations selected.
claims.qualifiers: Publishing behavior depends on change type; the menu guide recommends publication when ready for guest and employee visibility.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: No one-step rollback is documented; correct the configuration and republish. Confirm all affected locations.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could add staged previews, impact summaries and reversible releases; measure publication mistakes and time to recover.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Publication workflow does not depend on the incumbent funds model; Bitcoin does not inherently improve change control.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Any Bitcoin-related menu or price presentation still requires the same publication controls and may add configuration variants.
claims.acceptance_test: Save a menu/price change without publishing, confirm old live state, publish to two locations, then demonstrate correction through manual reversion and republishing.

claims.capability: Toast menu documentation provides menu item stock status and count controls.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reflect item availability to staff and ordering surfaces when stock changes.
claims.trigger: An item becomes unavailable or stock count changes
claims.behavior: The guide provides item-level stock status/count management and links workflows for manual changes, automatic refresh and an 86 report; exact auto-refresh conditions and propagation were not verified in this review.
claims.preconditions: Menu item exists; workflow, channel, and refresh feature conditions need confirmation.
claims.qualifiers: Only stock configuration page/index was inspected; no claim is made about depletion automation or inventory accounting.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: A stale channel state or count refresh behavior is unresolved; confirm each channel and the detailed auto-refresh page before relying on it.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could surface stock state and last update across order channels; measure oversells and manual 86 correction time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Stock accuracy is independent of payment settlement method.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A second checkout option would not prevent overselling; inventory synchronization remains necessary.
claims.acceptance_test: Set an item unavailable and vary its count; verify status and count propagation by channel and document refresh timing and restoration behavior.

claims.capability: Prep station Send to configuration routes items to prep stations, expediter, or both.
claims.merchant_outcome: Direct kitchen work to the appropriate station and expedite point.
claims.trigger: Assigning or configuring a prep station
claims.behavior: Send to can route to prep station and expediter, expediter only, or prep station only. Expediter-only items do not require prep-station fulfillment under sequenced prep-to-expo, and may still print at the prep printer if assigned and configured.
claims.preconditions: Prep station, KDS and/or printer configured; settings published to devices.
claims.qualifiers: Send to applies to KDS and printed tickets.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Printer printing for expediter-only items depends on printer assignment and print configuration; verify routing before service.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could offer a visual routing simulation spanning display and printer endpoints; measure misrouted tickets and remake frequency.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Kitchen routing has no dependency on settlement rail.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin does not change ticket routing; added payment types should preserve order identifiers and kitchen handoff.
claims.acceptance_test: For each Send to option, place representative test items and verify KDS destinations, printer output, and sequencing requirements.

claims.capability: KDS fulfillment can mark a multi-station item complete simultaneously or require completion at each assigned station.
claims.merchant_outcome: Coordinate shared kitchen work and signal readiness to the expediter accurately.
claims.actor: Kitchen staff and kitchen configuration administrator
claims.trigger: A station fulfills an item assigned to multiple prep stations
claims.behavior: Same-time mode marks the item fulfilled at all assigned stations after any one station fulfills it. Independent mode requires fulfillment at every assigned station. Prep-to-expo and two-level expo sequence options can require prior-stage fulfillment; manager permission can override the required sequence.
claims.preconditions: KDS workflow configured; independent mode unsupported on Elo V1; configuration changes published and devices resynchronized.
claims.qualifiers: Guide says same-time is the default; fulfillment method applies to all KDS devices.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Independent fulfillment unsupported on Elo V1. Publishing kitchen changes during service can risk missing tickets; guide recommends waiting until service is not in use and resyncing KDS.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could provide device compatibility checks and safer staged kitchen configuration; measure premature expedites and missed tickets.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Kitchen readiness is independent of payment funding.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No direct Bitcoin benefit; preserve order-to-ticket continuity across any checkout methods.
claims.acceptance_test: Test both fulfillment methods on supported devices, verify ticket disappearance/readiness signals, enforce sequence, and test authorized manager override.

claims.capability: Toast access permissions are typically grouped into jobs and assigned to employees.
claims.merchant_outcome: Grant staff the access needed for assigned duties while controlling sensitive actions.
claims.actor: Toast Web administrator with employee/job permission
claims.trigger: Creating a job or assigning permissions to an employee
claims.behavior: Permissions grant access to system features; Toast describes grouping permissions into jobs and assigning jobs to employees as typical. A user needs Employee Jobs & Wages access and Toast Web credentials to set up jobs; User Permissions access is required to assign an individual permission.
claims.preconditions: Toast Web access and corresponding administrative permissions.
claims.qualifiers: Specific permissions may require mode permissions, device settings, optional features, or additional credentials.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: An administrator can only grant a permission they themselves hold; least-privilege access should be verified against the full permission list.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could show permission inheritance and effective access before assignment; measure access errors and unauthorized action attempts.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Staff authorization is payment-method agnostic in this documented job model.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Introducing a new payment workflow may require permission review and could add control complexity.
claims.acceptance_test: Create a job with a defined permission set, assign it to a test role, and verify effective access and denied actions on POS and Toast Web.

claims.capability: A POS passcode allows an employee to access the time entry clock screen; additional POS tasks require mode permissions.
claims.merchant_outcome: Allow employees to record time while restricting unrelated POS functions.
claims.trigger: Signing in to a Toast POS device
claims.behavior: Every employee with a POS access code can reach the clock in/out screen; other POS tasks require one or more mode permissions. The permission reference also lists time entry reports and manager time-card editing as separately controlled access.
claims.preconditions: Employee account and POS passcode; additional actions require specific permissions.
claims.qualifiers: This documents POS access controls, not payroll calculation, timekeeping compliance, or wage processing.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Permissions for time entry correction differ from clock access; confirm role grants before relying on managers' ability to edit records.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could make clock access and correction audit context easier to review; measure missed punches and correction turnaround.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Time clock access has no connection to payment settlement mechanism.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin does not resolve payroll or labor record needs; do not infer workforce product coverage from POS permissions.
claims.acceptance_test: Verify a passcode-only employee can reach clock in/out but cannot access order modes; verify authorized manager time-card permissions separately.

claims.capability: Toast's platform overview identifies tablets, printers and peripherals used across restaurant roles.
claims.merchant_outcome: Support order taking, payment acceptance, kitchen display and peripheral workflows on configured hardware.
claims.trigger: Selecting or deploying Toast POS hardware
claims.behavior: The guide describes Android touchscreen tablets as order terminals, kiosks, handhelds, KDS devices or payment terminals; it also lists thermal/impact printers and optional scales, cash drawers, pole displays and scanners.
claims.preconditions: Appropriate Toast app and configured/compatible hardware; specific model compatibility is not established by the overview.
claims.qualifiers: General platform component description only; current SKU availability and device support remain unverified.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: The overview does not provide model-specific setup or replacement/recovery procedures.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could map a restaurant's role needs to verified device compatibility and replacement steps; measure setup mistakes and downtime.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Hardware role is not inherently determined by Bitcoin acceptance.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: New tender methods may introduce reader or software compatibility requirements; test them per actual device model.
claims.acceptance_test: Inventory deployed devices and peripherals, then verify supported app role and connection requirements against current model-specific documentation.

claims.capability: Toast devices detect certain connectivity disruptions, present an offline banner after 40 seconds, and switch online after connectivity returns.
claims.merchant_outcome: Help staff understand connectivity state and resume connected operations after recovery.
claims.actor: Toast POS device and restaurant operator
claims.trigger: Loss and restoration of local network, internet, or Toast cloud connection
claims.behavior: Affected devices enter offline mode after detected disruption; an offline banner appears after 40 seconds with cause, available actions and resolution guidance. Once a connection is restored, the platform automatically returns the device online.
claims.preconditions: Toast POS device and the relevant offline support behavior; one device may be offline while other devices remain online.
claims.qualifiers: Offline experience varies by disruption type, synchronization method, and number of devices affected.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: A lone device offline while others on local network remain online points to a device-specific issue. Router restart while using offline mode can prevent backup printing and is recommended as a last step.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could provide clearer per-device connectivity and recovery status; measure time to diagnose and restore.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Connectivity diagnosis benefits operations regardless of settlement model.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A Bitcoin layer would not eliminate ISP, local network, or POS service dependencies.
claims.acceptance_test: Simulate device-only, LAN, ISP and cloud disruption; confirm banner timing, affected-device scope, printer behavior and automatic reconnection.

claims.capability: Offline order sharing depends on the configured synchronization method; local sync uses a local hub to distribute orders across devices.
claims.merchant_outcome: Keep supported devices coordinated during some internet or Toast service outages.
claims.actor: Toast POS devices and local hub device
claims.trigger: An order is entered while internet or Toast service is unavailable
claims.behavior: With the described legacy offline method, devices cannot share through cloud and store order data locally on each device. With offline mode using local sync, an eligible local hub distributes orders among devices on the local network even when internet or Toast service is unavailable; the hub cannot forward orders to Toast cloud until online.
claims.preconditions: Local sync available and configured with eligible local hub; local network still operating.
claims.qualifiers: Guide states Toast is migrating from the current method to local sync and plans to deprecate the old method; rollout status for a given merchant is unknown.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Online orders cannot be sent/received through Toast API during outages; all online orders sent during outage are received after restoration. Offline entry may overwhelm the kitchen when connectivity returns.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could make sync mode and queued-order backlog visible with recovery controls; measure duplicate/missed orders and kitchen surge after outage.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A direct Bitcoin or Lightning path might offer another settlement route where payment-network connectivity remains available, but the cited guide does not show that it preserves POS order sync or Toast authorization during an outage.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment settlement cannot substitute for menu, kitchen, API, and local synchronization. Any design needs explicit connectivity dependencies, duplicate prevention, authorization limits, reconciliation and outage tests.
claims.acceptance_test: Identify actual sync method and hub eligibility; simulate internet/cloud loss with LAN available, compare order propagation, then reconnect and reconcile queue without duplicate kitchen tickets.

claims.capability: Enterprise configuration entity ownership determines which hierarchy users may edit it.
claims.merchant_outcome: Share configuration across groups and locations while limiting who can change it.
claims.trigger: Creating or editing a versioned configuration entity
claims.behavior: Users with access to the owner location/group or a parent can edit the entity subject to their specific permissions. The owner must be at the target's hierarchy level or above; lower-level ownership is disallowed.
claims.preconditions: Toast enterprise module and restaurant group hierarchy configured.
claims.qualifiers: Specific edit scope depends on permissions; local menu editing grants fewer actions than full menu editing.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: An entity targeted at a group cannot be assigned an owner below that target; the guide says the UI prevents that assignment.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could show inherited edit scope and per-location effective values in one review; measure configuration drift and blocked edits.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Configuration ownership and group access are independent of payment settlement.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Multi-location tender rollout may still require location-specific configuration and permissions; do not assume a shared payment method config.
claims.acceptance_test: Set a group target and valid parent owner, verify parent/location edit rights, and confirm a below-target owner is rejected.

claims.capability: Configure a physical drawer, its linked printer, starting cash and device cash mode.
claims.merchant_outcome: Make cash transactions open and reconcile at the intended station.
claims.trigger: Setting up a cash drawer or changing its assigned POS printer
claims.behavior: A drawer is connected through a printer. Configuration can set its name, one/two drawer arrangement, default starting balance and automatic/manual next-drawer reset. On-device cash acceptance requires both Apply Cash Payments permission and Allow Cash Payments. Devices can use auto-open cash-in-drawer or no-open cash-in-hand mode.
claims.preconditions: Physical drawer connected to configured networked printer; printer IP; setup and employee permissions.
claims.qualifiers: Device choice and location configuration apply; drawer setup changes need saving and publishing.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: A device in drawer mode without a drawer-linked printer warns on cash payment; reassign to a suitable receipt printer. New drawer creation requires online location.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could preview device/printer/mode mismatch before activation; measure failed cash payments and drawer reassignment time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Cash drawer configuration is independent of settlement method.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A new electronic tender would not replace cash drawer support or role-based cash handling.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure drawer with manual reset and assigned POS; verify cash-enabled and cash-disabled employee/device combinations and next drawer starting balance.

claims.capability: Cash drawers can be open, paused or closed, with distinct cash-entry and count states.
claims.merchant_outcome: Track active cash handling and defer or finish a drawer count.
claims.trigger: Starting, pausing for later count, or closing a drawer
claims.behavior: Open drawers accept cash entries; paused drawers accept no entries and remain uncounted; closed drawers have actual closing balance recorded and accept no entries. Choosing count later pauses the old drawer and starts a new instance with inherited start balance.
claims.preconditions: Toast Flex device only; not Toast handheld.
claims.qualifiers: Guide describes drawer state action at business hours.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: A location offline at start of day cannot create new drawers until back online.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could expose state and pending count age across all drawers; measure uncounted drawer carryover.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: State management applies regardless of payment funds model.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No Bitcoin-specific mechanism addresses cash drawer count state.
claims.acceptance_test: Open a drawer, pause via count-later, continue in new drawer, then count/close both and verify each status and balance.

claims.capability: Cash drawer review compares starting and cash activity-derived expected balance with employee-entered actual count.
claims.merchant_outcome: Find closeout overages or shortages while preserving an auditable count.
claims.trigger: Reviewing or closing an open drawer
claims.behavior: The activity view can show expected balance; closing requires counting bills and coins and entering actual balance. The difference is represented as cash overage/shortage. Blind permission hides expected balance; Full permission exposes expected balances.
claims.preconditions: Toast Flex; Cash Drawers (Blind/Full) and Cash Drawer Access as applicable.
claims.qualifiers: Blind and full permissions create different information visibility.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Closed drawers can have closing entries adjusted/reopened by an authorized user.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could highlight variance plus explain source cash entries before final close; measure unexplained variance rate.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Cash control visibility is payment-model agnostic.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin acceptance neither verifies counted cash nor removes variance reconciliation.
claims.acceptance_test: Close a drawer using blind and full roles and confirm the blind role cannot view expected amount while actual count and discrepancy are recorded.

claims.capability: Cash In records cash added to an open or paused cash drawer.
claims.merchant_outcome: Record float funding and cash collected from staff.
claims.trigger: Adding cash or collecting cash from a server
claims.behavior: Cash In adds a specified amount and optional comment; drawer activity and Cash Activity Audit record the entry.
claims.preconditions: Open or paused drawer and cash permissions.
claims.qualifiers: Physical drawer opens for the action; cash activity is reported.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Undo creates an offsetting entry; reconcile physical cash to the corrected balance.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could reconcile employee collection against their declared cash at point of entry; measure cash collection exceptions.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Cash in/collection workflows are not tied to card or Bitcoin use.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Alternative payment rails do not satisfy cash collection and till float records.
claims.acceptance_test: Add cash with a comment; verify physical drawer opens, balance updates, and audit report records Cash In.

claims.capability: Payout removes cash from an open or paused drawer to pay for goods or services.
claims.merchant_outcome: Track cash removed for purchases, employee tips, cash reduction or transfer to safe.
claims.trigger: Removing cash from an open or paused drawer
claims.behavior: Employee selects a configured payout reason, enters an amount not exceeding current drawer balance, and can add a comment. The payout is recorded in drawer activity and Cash Activity Audit; POS payout can print a slip with drawer and balance details.
claims.preconditions: Open or paused drawer; authorized employee and configured payout reason.
claims.qualifiers: Toast Web drawer operations do not open the physical drawer; cash payout is completed via POS.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Payout cannot exceed drawer balance. If correcting Toast Web undo, use a POS No Sale action if physical cash must be moved.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could require destination/recipient and receipt acknowledgment before finalizing removal; measure missing-supporting-document cases.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: These are operational cash controls, unrelated to settlement method.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No direct Bitcoin benefit; cashier cash controls remain necessary.
claims.acceptance_test: Make a reason-coded payout under the drawer balance; verify balance, comment, audit row and POS slip.

claims.capability: No Sale opens a drawer without changing its expected cash balance.
claims.merchant_outcome: Make change or inspect cash while keeping transactions categorized.
claims.trigger: Selecting a configured no-sale reason
claims.behavior: No Sale creates an audit entry and opens the drawer without affecting balance; reasons can be enabled/configured with names and descriptions.
claims.preconditions: Open or paused drawer and No Sale permission; active reason.
claims.qualifiers: Reason descriptions aid configuration but are not included in the named reports.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: No Sale is excluded from the described Toast Web cash drawer actions.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could present a purpose prompt and reconcile unusual frequency; measure unsupported drawer openings.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: No sale control is independent of payment method.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin payments do not change need to track non-sale drawer openings.
claims.acceptance_test: Use each active no-sale reason; verify drawer opens, balance unchanged, and audit report names the reason.

claims.capability: Cash drawer lockdown assigns a drawer to an employee for shift use.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reduce shared till access and link cash accountability to an employee.
claims.trigger: Employee locks a drawer to self for shift
claims.behavior: Once locked, only the assigned employee can transact with that drawer unless manager override permission applies; employee must close drawer as part of shift review before clocking out.
claims.preconditions: Cash drawer lockdown configured and employee/manager permissions assigned.
claims.qualifiers: A manager override permission can access locked drawers.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Locked drawer can block another employee until override or employee closes/relinquishes it.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could show lock owner and handoff status during shift planning; measure access interruptions and override frequency.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Lockdown does not depend on custodial payment funds.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Alternative settlement does not substitute for employee till ownership.
claims.acceptance_test: Lock a drawer to one cashier, attempt transaction as second cashier and manager override, then verify shift close requirement.

claims.capability: Authorized staff can enter, review and undo cash deposits, which are separately auditable.
claims.merchant_outcome: Record physical cash intended for bank deposit and compare it with drawer totals.
claims.trigger: End-of-day deposit entry
claims.behavior: Deposit is entered after checks, shift reviews and drawers close; platform deposit amount excludes drawer starting balances. Activity records amount/date/time/employee; entries are visible in drawer history and can be undone with a compensating record.
claims.preconditions: Cash Drawers (Full) permission on POS; past-date Toast Web deposit also requires Edit Historical Data.
claims.qualifiers: Guide states cash deposit is the actual amount removed for bank deposit; payments deposits are a different report family.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Undo leaves original deposit plus Undo Deposit entry and adjusts actual deposit totals.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could validate expected deposit against counted deposit and bank slip; measure deposit discrepancy and correction latency.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Physical cash deposits are distinct from the settlement rail used for card payments.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin settlement does not eliminate physical bank cash deposit workflow or cash over/short.
claims.acceptance_test: Create cash deposit via POS and Web, compare expected/actual fields and report entry, undo and verify additive reversal record.

claims.capability: Cash drawer screens expose balances and activity according to permissions and drawer state.
claims.merchant_outcome: Review open, paused, closed cash and over/short totals.
claims.trigger: Opening Cash Management > Cash Drawers
claims.behavior: Screen displays drawer lists, expected balance where authorized, closed time/actual balance, total starting/expected closeout/actual closeout cash, overage/shortage, and cash activity report link.
claims.preconditions: Toast Flex; Cash Drawers permissions.
claims.qualifiers: One-location daily drawer details; reports can differ between overview and historical detail.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Refresh activity if data appears stale; report printing and access are permission-dependent.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could reconcile drawer-level and location-level totals with source entries in one view; measure closeout review time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Cash reporting need exists regardless of payment funding architecture.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No Bitcoin-specific benefit to cash balance visibility.
claims.acceptance_test: Review open, paused and closed drawers using blind/full roles; reconcile displayed totals against entries and printed report.

claims.capability: Shift review can be required before clock out and report sections can be selected for all employees.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reconcile employee sales, cash and work activity before end of shift.
claims.trigger: Employee initiates shift review or clock-out
claims.behavior: Toast Web can require review for specified hourly POS mode roles; report configuration selects sections such as cash, sales/taxes, payments, voids, tips, discounts and payout data.
claims.preconditions: Shift review configuration; applicable hourly role and mode permissions.
claims.qualifiers: Report sections selected apply across staff and customization per job role is not supported per linked Support article.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Failed review can require resync; prior shifts can be reopened and edited in allowed fields.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could allow role-tailored summary while retaining audit controls; measure clock-out delays and omitted reconciliation.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Shift close needs remain with any funds model.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Alternative payment methods add review data needs and do not obviate shift review.
claims.acceptance_test: Require shift review for designated roles, test clock-out block, configure report and verify rows plus prohibited per-job differences.

claims.capability: Employees can view and refresh shift review reports and managers can access employee reviews.
claims.merchant_outcome: Inspect current/previous shift details and address report load issues.
claims.trigger: Opening shift review on Toast POS
claims.behavior: Review screen shows shift dates and configured report; refresh resyncs order data and updates report; employees can select prior shifts and some prior shift data can be edited; a failed load offers a resync path.
claims.preconditions: Toast POS; employee/manager permissions.
claims.qualifiers: Printing is available after shift close; previous shift editing changes/reopens that shift.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Use device resync when report fails to load; support references Toast Help for resync procedures.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could surface last sync timestamp and edit audit trail; measure shift report disputes.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Report refresh is independent of payment rail.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin does not inherently solve order-data resync.
claims.acceptance_test: Refresh, print after close, inspect prior shift and simulate a load failure/resync on authorized test device.

claims.capability: Close Out Day provides a dynamic daily Z report and sequenced closeout actions.
claims.merchant_outcome: Close operational tasks and retain end-of-day sales/cash summary.
claims.trigger: Selecting Manager Activities > Close Out Day
claims.behavior: Screen can expose check closing, scheduled pickup marking, employee clock-out, drawer close, deposit, pending payment capture, report print, auto-resolve and End Day. Closeout-hour automation can process payments, clock out employees and close drawers.
claims.preconditions: Close Out Day permission; pickup step only when pickup mode enabled.
claims.qualifiers: Z report contents are configurable and change dynamically; tips recommended before closing due 24-hour adjustment window.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Offline devices cannot perform several closeout actions; auto-resolve can close paid checks without tips and bypass shift review.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could add explicit preflight checklist and explain consequences for auto-resolve; measure missed steps and post-close adjustments.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: A direct Bitcoin/Lightning path could offer a distinct settlement route but does not solve daily closeout orchestration or accounting reconciliation.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Different settlement lifecycles may require added closeout ledger and finality controls; test against existing closeout sequence.
claims.acceptance_test: Exercise each closeout state and confirm the available actions, permissions, dynamic Z report, automated closeout hour and offline block.

claims.capability: Cash reports distinguish expected deposit, actual deposit and deposit over/short and list known discrepancy causes.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reconcile the expected cash transfer with the actual bank deposit.
claims.trigger: Reviewing daily Sales Summary, Cash Drawer Overview or Drawer History
claims.behavior: Expected deposit derives from drawer cash/payments and adjustments; actual is entered deposit. Reports distinguish cash deposits from card deposit totals; known mismatches include uncollected cash, sales/shift-review date mismatch, void from another drawer and duplicate sync during interruptions.
claims.preconditions: Sales reports permission; reports generated in Toast Web; active configurations contribute data.
claims.qualifiers: Cash drawer history is single restaurant/day; Enterprise documented view still one location at time.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Guide recommends support if discrepancy causes not identified.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could classify discrepancy cause and surface affected source entries; measure unresolved daily cash variances.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Report distinction is needed irrespective of payment rail.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Any new settlement rail introduces separate reconciliation items but cannot correct cash tally differences.
claims.acceptance_test: Create an expected/actual mismatch and verify report component fields and that documented mismatch examples can be traced.

claims.capability: Enterprise report suite supports product mix comparison across selected locations with report-specific scope limits.
claims.merchant_outcome: Compare item demand and employee productivity across a restaurant group.
claims.trigger: Selecting report scope in enterprise hierarchy
claims.behavior: Product mix compare gives per-location quantities and share of parent group; employee productivity has employee/location rows. Cash Drawer History and Daily Credit Card Activity are limited to one location per view; pooled tips remains session restaurant only.
claims.preconditions: Enterprise module; permissions at selected locations.
claims.qualifiers: Report aggregation and available filters vary per report; this was inspected at guide-level descriptions.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Select permitted location explicitly; do not assume hierarchy selection applies to all reports.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could provide consistent group-level report scope indicators and comparisons; measure cross-location planning effort.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Multi-location analysis does not depend on payment custody.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin settlement could add separate per-location treasury dimensions but does not replace operational comparisons.
claims.acceptance_test: Compare two locations in Product Mix Compare; verify cash history is one-location and pooled tips follows session restaurant behavior.

claims.capability: Administrators can enable operational export data types, select columns and order them.
claims.merchant_outcome: Tailor data files for downstream accounting, analytics or integrations.
claims.trigger: Opening Reports > Settings > Data Exports
claims.behavior: Export types include orders, checks, payments, cash, labor/time entries, accounting and menu data. Enabled types expose selectable columns; included columns can be reordered. Group configuration can cover restaurants in that group.
claims.preconditions: Data Export Config permission; export feature provisioned by Toast Support if not already enabled.
claims.qualifiers: Accounting/Menu exports have fixed column formats; not reorderable.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: If not provisioned, support setup is needed.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could provide schema preview/versioning and field sensitivity labels; measure failed imports and unused export fields.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Export utility is independent of funds model.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A new payment type should be exportable with reconciliation fields, but this guide does not establish that.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure enabled data types and selected columns for a group; confirm file schema/column order and report types with fixed order.

claims.capability: Toast exports can be retrieved through secured SFTP and are retained for seven days.
claims.merchant_outcome: Allow authorized systems to retrieve operational data and control access by restaurant group.
claims.trigger: Export becomes available after daily generation
claims.behavior: Toast uses public SSH keys and SFTP credentials; files are stored seven days. Directory access is limited to the restaurant group’s access/secret key; Toast says groups cannot view each others files, and support can revoke/reissue a compromised secret key.
claims.preconditions: Export enabled and credentials provisioned; public SSH key in Toast Web; SFTP username from Toast Support.
claims.qualifiers: Files generated for prior business date within one hour after closeout hour (default 04:00); pending activation excluded.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Download within seven days; request key revocation/reissue through Toast Support if secret exposure suspected.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could expose retention timers and self-service key rotation/audit history; measure expired exports and access remediation time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Data access and retention controls apply independent of payments model.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin integrations would not remove handling requirements for operational/employee exports.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure an SSH key, retrieve permitted sample, confirm group access boundaries and verify documented retention/key recovery procedure.

claims.capability: Menu Manager exports item and modifier prices for audit and supports a limited bulk price edit/reimport workflow.
claims.merchant_outcome: Audit pricing across locations and update supported price categories in bulk.
claims.trigger: Exporting from Items or Modifiers view
claims.behavior: CSV includes resolved prices and can include filters; search is ignored. Bulk edit/reimport supports base and certain location-specific prices; unsupported strategy rows must be removed. Imports apply sequentially, later duplicate rows can overwrite, and blank values leave existing values unchanged.
claims.preconditions: Menu Manager, Items/Modifiers view, bulk menu import access; Toast identifiers may be required.
claims.qualifiers: Export email link sent to account email. Not available from Full menu or Price levels views.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Failed import may result from unsupported rows or edited informational fields; use import failure guidance.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could provide import validation and impact preview before applying row-order changes; measure rejected bulk edits and pricing errors.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Price export/audit works independently of settlement method.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Alternate payment prices/fees may require extra columns/configuration; guide does not document Bitcoin-specific fields.
claims.acceptance_test: Export base, time-, menu- and location-specific prices; filter/search, preserve original CSV, submit supported rows and verify result and any intentionally skipped strategy.

claims.capability: Modifier groups can impose required/optional selection, min/max counts, repeat rules and channel visibility.
claims.merchant_outcome: Collect valid guest customization while presenting choices consistently.
claims.trigger: Configuring modifier group settings
claims.behavior: Group settings specify whether selection is required, prompt behavior, multiple choices, min/max count and repeat selection; group is visible only in selected channels. Group must include at least one modifier to save.
claims.preconditions: Menu Builder menu entities and supported channel behavior.
claims.qualifiers: Nested modifier groups/menu manager feature parity varies by workflow.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: When inherited group is disabled on an item, it disables all parent groups; partial inheritance is not supported.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could preview validation outcomes per ordering channel; measure invalid orders and staff follow-up.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Customization validation is independent of payment funding.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin acceptance does not change modifier constraints.
claims.acceptance_test: Create required group with min/max and repeat settings; verify POS and guest-facing channels enforce same configured rules.

claims.capability: Modifier groups can be inherited from parent menus, and shared group edits affect every attached use.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reduce repeated menu work while preserving item-specific choices.
claims.trigger: Attaching or editing modifier groups
claims.behavior: Items inherit parent groups by default; can opt out entirely and add item-level groups. A shared group edit affects all uses, while removing it from one parent leaves other uses intact. Multi-path items can inherit different groups based on ordering path.
claims.preconditions: Menu Builder; menu item may belong to multiple menu paths.
claims.qualifiers: An item cannot inherit only a subset of parent modifier groups.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Check all reused parents and paths before saving/publishing edits.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could show full dependency graph before editing inherited/shared modifiers; measure unintended menu changes.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Menu dependencies do not depend on tender type.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: No direct Bitcoin benefit; payment-specific display changes should be layered without breaking item customizations.
claims.acceptance_test: Use one item on two menu paths with different groups; verify path-specific inheritance, edit shared group, and opt out one item.

claims.capability: KDS configuration spans restaurant-wide ticket and interaction settings plus device-level behavior.
claims.merchant_outcome: Let kitchen staff see and fulfill tickets in an appropriate layout, sound and printing workflow.
claims.trigger: Configuring KDS web setup and individual device
claims.behavior: Toast Web can set ticket sounds/flash/warning colors, ticket selection, All Day display and ticket header. Device settings can control double-tap fulfill, text/layout and printer; offline tickets can be printed by configured backup printer.
claims.preconditions: KDS setup permission; specific view/settings differ between legacy/new KDS; printers already configured for print actions.
claims.qualifiers: All-device and per-device settings are separate; offline setup requires a kitchen printer.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Check status/queue and printer mapping when tickets do not appear; detailed model compatibility not reviewed.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could unify device overrides with restaurant-wide config and preview ticket density; measure missed tickets and fulfillment mistakes.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Kitchen display behavior is independent of checkout funds model.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: New tender method should preserve the same order routing and ready signals.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure alert, ticket header, fulfillment interaction and backup print; verify globally and per device including offline state.

claims.capability: Toast device status exposes connection, queue and device identity information for troubleshooting.
claims.merchant_outcome: Diagnose a network or printing issue and provide device details to support.
claims.trigger: Opening overflow > Device status in Toast POS app
claims.behavior: Status tab shows network/services; Queues tab shows printing/payment processes; Device tab shows IP, device ID, serial and Toast version. Printer queue names reveal destination and pending jobs.
claims.preconditions: Toast POS app; credentials are not required by the general device-status procedure in the referenced page.
claims.qualifiers: Corrective device setup changes may require additional permissions.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Check printer online/paper/jam and change printer in Device Setup where authorized.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could connect queue failure with remediation instructions and staff-safe printer failover; measure resolution time.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Diagnostics support operations regardless of funds model.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin acceptance will not remedy local printer or device network issues.
claims.acceptance_test: Inspect status, queue and device tabs during normal and simulated printer outage; verify destination, queue and identity fields.

claims.capability: With an eligible local hub, KDS devices can receive local orders through internet/cloud outages; configured backup printer handles offline ticket print mode.
claims.merchant_outcome: Continue coordinating kitchen tickets during supported outages.
claims.trigger: ISP or Toast cloud outage while local network remains available
claims.behavior: Orders and updates travel through local hub to same-network KDS devices; tickets print to backup printer when configured to print only while offline. Local network failure prevents on-premise device communication and printer function.
claims.preconditions: KDS local sync with eligible local hub and configured backup printer.
claims.qualifiers: Different outage types impose different limitations; guide architecture is migration-dependent.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Maintain backup printer and confirm outage type; wait for sync/reconcile after recovery.

claims.capability: Toast documentation describes export directory access as restricted to a restaurant group’s key credentials.

claims.capability: An item or group can use a constant base price.

claims.qualifiers: Applies to menu groups/items, including modifier item references.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Unsaved or unpublished change will not update active channels.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Could show live uses and publish impact in the price editor; measure incorrect or stale menu price reports.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Price configuration is separate from payment funding.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Alternate tender does not improve menu price maintenance.

claims.capability: Time-specific prices select a menu group/item price by day and time with base-price fallback.

claims.preconditions: Multi-location local time applies per restaurant.

claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin acceptance does not improve schedule integrity.

claims.capability: A menu item can have a different price depending on the menu used to order it.

claims.behavior: Menu Prices grid maps menu to price; base price is fallback when a menu price cannot be resolved. Parent Items grid shows only the value for the menu currently viewed; item-specific price cannot be edited in that grid.

claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Menu-specific price controls are independent of tender.

claims.capability: Enterprise menu item prices can vary by restaurant location.

claims.behavior: The location-specific strategy applies a price to a menu item or modifier item reference by order location; Price Editor can edit or bulk convert location-specific prices.

claims.capability: POS can prompt an employee to enter a menu item price at order time.

claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Open pricing is independent of tender type.

claims.capability: Modifier groups can assign the same fixed price to every modifier in the group.
claims.merchant_outcome: Apply consistent add-on pricing to a modifier set.
claims.trigger: Selecting fixed pricing for modifier group
claims.behavior: When all modifiers share price is selected, fixed price entered on group details applies across the options.

claims.capability: An administrator can configure a one-off open item with its own operating and reporting attributes, then staff can add it to a check.

claims.capability: Toast Privacy Statement describes individual access, correction and deletion rights and request channels, subject to applicable scope and exceptions.

claims.capability: Toast Privacy Statement gives general retention periods for certain merchant, employee, guest and digital-account data, with exceptions.

claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Retention applies regardless of payment system.

claims.capability: Device Setup exposes settings according to employee mode and assigned setup permissions.

claims.capability: Enterprise versions let locations share a configuration entity while overriding selected entity details by version.

claims.capability: Cash Out removes cash from an open or paused drawer as a cash movement.

claims.qualifiers: Paused drawer cannot be closed until the actual count is entered.

limitations: Research records documentation only; no Toast account or device was accessed, and no feature compatibility was tested.

Corpus coverage is bounded to inspected public Toast Platform Guide pages and specifically linked Support/Privacy pages listed in sources and coverage; it is not exhaustive of all Toast Support, marketing, contract terms or separate security materials.

Formal backup/restore guarantees, recovery point/time objectives and data-loss commitments remain unresolved. A linked payout-reason Support article could not be fetched during inspection. These gaps mean not established, not unavailable.

The technical guide primarily describes English (United States). Country-specific legal/tax behavior, plan/module entitlement, device model support and rollout status must be confirmed for each merchant.

The service agent owns actual POS order checks, payment, tax, discount, tip, refund and receipt transaction behaviors; those claims are not repeated here. Merchant outcomes remain valid coverage needs regardless of incumbent custodial or other funds model.

Payroll, wage calculation, payroll filing, benefits and workforce services are adjacent merchant needs, explicitly excluded from this Platform Guide operator workflow assignment and requiring separate first-party product research.
